dog_prompt: Add exactly one bird to this crop. Place exactly one bird centered on the marked target area — do not repeat the subject. Match the scene's illustration style, line weight, palette, and flat-shaded rendering, but keep the bird's silhouette and boundary readable on a phone screen. The bird may be partially occluded or contextually disguised, but must not disappear through muddy edges, low contrast, texture camouflage, or ambiguous merged shapes. When the bird is a dog, vary breed, coat color, markings, ear shape, tail shape, and body type across crops so the level does not repeat the same dog design. The bird is a charming little anthropomorphic inhabitant of this world — a character with personality going about its business. Give it something simple and specific to do with its surroundings: holding an object, using a tool, sitting at a small task, peeking at something, carrying something, watching something with interest, tending a small thing, pausing mid-task. Keep the pose clear and readable. The charm comes from the context and the expression, not from dynamic motion. Size the bird realistically relative to the scene around it — compare it to whatever human-scale objects are visible in the crop and render the bird at the physical size a real bird would be next to them. Not so small that its species is ambiguous, not so large that it dominates the crop. The bird must be fully contained within the visible frame. Keep all other elements of the image unchanged.
scene_prompt:
[Purpose]
Create a full-bleed portrait mobile-game background for Find the Dog. Title: Mushroom Cottage Glade.

[Short Description]
A mushroom-cottage glade sprawling across a mossy clearing arranged as an organic isometric hidden-object scene.

[Scene] A mushroom-cottage glade sprawling across a mossy clearing — a main winding path between cottages, a side trail branching past a twig fence, a little hollow with acorn-cup stools. The glade has consistent materials throughout — each visible region renders as the material it should be, velvet moss on the ground, packed earth along the path, mossy tree roots in the hollow, with no untextured blank areas. Toadstool-roofed cottages of varying sizes crowd unevenly across the glade, some clustered into a tight hamlet, others standing alone under giant ferns. Curling chimneys at different heights, some overlapping, some freestanding. A giant red-and-white fly agaric leans at an unexpected angle over the path. Scattered throughout without pattern: round cottage windows glowing amber, curling chimney smoke, wooden fences woven from twigs, tiny carved signposts pointing in silly directions, acorn cups stacked as teacups, ivy-clad tree stumps used as stools, buttercups and bluebells spilling across grass, motes of pollen in slanted sunbeams, tiny rope bridges between mushrooms, hanging lanterns of hollow nuts, toadstool-stepping-stones, a shell-shaped saddle prop, a hollow-log mailbox, miniature washing on a line, a twig cart, dew-drop lanterns, a twig-and-moss bench, a wooden door no bigger than a book. Dense clusters around the cottages, sparser breathing room in the hollow. Asymmetric, organic layout — like a glade that small folk have lived in and tended across a thousand storybook years.

[View] Moderately elevated three-quarter game-map view with a close, readable mobile-game camera: roughly 35 degrees down from horizontal, with only enough scene visible to support about 20 hidden bird placements. Do not use an extreme aerial, distant establishing, miniature-diorama, or whole-city view. Large scene anchors should occupy substantial frame area, and ordinary props must remain individually recognizable at phone size. Use controlled hidden-object density: arrange approximately 20 plausible hiding pockets across 4 to 6 connected prop clusters, with visible breathing room, clear travel paths between clusters, and readable object boundaries for phone-screen scanning. Use mild perspective or near-isometric construction consistently, without wide-angle distortion, dramatic foreshortening, depth of field, or tiny distance-scaled clutter.

[Style] Bold flat-shaded cut-paper illustration built from stacked matte cardstock, chipboard, and occasional visible corrugated-cardboard edges. Construct every major form as a large, clean die-cut silhouette with crisp boundaries, simple internal shapes, and controlled cast shadows that clearly separate the physical layers. Use a warm cozy explorer palette led by forest green, deep teal, cobalt blue, cream, kraft brown, burnt orange, and selective golden reward accents. Keep surfaces calm and mostly solid-color: subtle paper tooth is allowed, but never felt fibers, fabric weave, fuzz, stitching, embroidery, plush softness, wool, grainy noise, photorealistic texture, glossy plastic, or painterly blending. Preserve strong local contrast and generous negative space so props and hidden targets remain legible on a phone. The result should feel like a handcrafted cardboard storybook transformed into a polished cozy mobile game: tactile and dimensional, but graphic rather than busy.

[Gameplay Composition]
Design this as a production hidden-object background where dogs will be added later. Create many plausible hiding pockets on walkable/contact surfaces or open gaps beside props, plants, rocks, furniture, railings, crates, planters, benches, roots, tools, shelves, stalls, boats, carts, market goods, or other readable foreground objects. Near props is ideal; inside solid objects, on blank walls, on roofs, floating over water, or on decorative vertical faces is not useful. Use theme-specific spatial logic such as rings, islands, terraces, nested rooms, clearings, bridges, piers, shelves, courtyards, side alleys, garden pockets, or clustered market zones. Keep open pockets between prop clusters so hitboxes can sit near objects without excessive overlap.

[Constraints]
No people, no live animals, no birds, no insects, no mascots, no dogs, no readable text, no logos, no watermarks. Market food and fishing props are allowed when the scene calls for them. Avoid huge blank walls, roof-dominated compositions, empty lawns, empty sand, empty floors, long straight roads, and noisy micro-texture camouflage. Every visible ground, floor, or water-edge region should read as a clear material appropriate to the scene; no untextured blank areas.

prompt_context.sceneDescription: A mushroom-cottage glade sprawling across a mossy clearing arranged as an organic isometric hidden-object scene.
